source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Globally Enables or Disables Hot-Plug support for the entire System.
If System has Hot-Plug capable Slots and this option set to Enabled, it provides a Setup screen for selecting PCI resource padding for Hot-Plug.
[Enabled/Disabled]

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. Function should be enabled/disabled successfully without any error
2. Guest OS should be installed successfully
3. Guest OS should have virtual function devices

original_test_intent: Validate the global BIOS PCI Hot-Plug Support Enabled/Disabled behavior, related PCI resource padding, and the source-required guest installation/virtual-function outcome; the source does not establish how these acceptance elements connect.
original_method: Preserve both source states and criteria, but do not execute until the owner defines whether physical device hot-plug is required, which PCI/SR-IOV hardware and padding policy apply, and how guest installation/VFs demonstrate this setting.
manual_activity: At minimum an engineer must change/verify BIOS settings and supervise save/reset; physical PCI insertion/removal may also be core, but the source does not say whether it is required.
required_inputs: Semantic decision linking Hot-Plug, guest installation and VFs
Exact hot-plug-capable slot/device and padding policy
Physical hot-plug required or explicitly excluded
Guest/hypervisor image, safe disk and drivers
safety_requirements: Do not install a guest until the target disk is verified unmounted, unprotected and approved.
Do not physically hot-plug hardware unless the resolved plan and platform procedure explicitly authorize it.
Drain workloads before global PCI configuration changes/reboots.
Keep BMC/OOB recovery and BIOS backup.
agent_execution_scope: After semantic resolution, prepare/execute approved software inventory, guest/hypervisor checks and evidence collection.
Compare per-state PCI resources and VF enumeration.
Do not infer the missing physical operation or assign the formal verdict.
engineer_actions: Resolve the intended acceptance model and physical-action boundary.
Approve and supervise BIOS changes, guest target and any hardware operation.
Review per-state evidence, restore baseline and issue PASS/FAIL.

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure defines a global PCI hot-plug/padding setting, while Criteria additionally require guest OS installation and virtual-function devices without specifying their relationship, expected per-state behavior or whether any physical hot-plug occurs. These distinct mechanisms do not yield a single executable acceptance contract.

blocked_analysis.analysis: This is not blocked merely by missing packages or project values. The necessary operation and acceptance semantics are unresolved, so executing either a physical hot-plug test or only a VF/guest test would guess and could lower coverage.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains its safety and potential partial-automation plan but tightens the unresolved semantic boundary to BLOCKED under V3.1.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Records a case-level engineering decision rather than inventing a global hot-plug policy.

review_improvement: Prevents a General Help test, a setting-only check, a physical hot-plug test and an SR-IOV guest test from being treated as interchangeable.
independent_technical_reasoning: PCIe hot-plug controls resource padding; SR-IOV VFs depend on device/firmware/driver/IOMMU and guest assignment. Because the source never states the causal/per-state contract or physical boundary, safe independent execution is not yet defined and BLOCKED is justified.
